after.headline: Five experts weigh artificial intelligence’s climate benefits against its environmental costs

after.headline: Lawyers discuss time savings and fairness risks from AI in international disputes
after.deck: An arbitration panel describes everyday uses alongside false evidence, hidden reasoning and the need for human checks.
after.what_happened: At Hong Kong Arbitration Week, a panel hosted by A&O Shearman discussed how content-generating AI is changing international commercial disputes. Participants described using it for document review, legal research and first drafts of legal papers.
after.why_it_matters: The panel identified faster work and possible cost savings, but warned that misuse can make proceedings less fair. Human oversight and clear disclosure of AI use remain central to its recommendations.
body_paragraphs: The account identifies risks including fabricated evidence, biased answers and lengthy submissions containing mistakes. Faster proceedings conducted only through documents can leave decision-makers less time to spot these problems.

The lawyers also note that advanced tools cost money and that time saved may be spent developing more complex arguments. They describe disclosure requirements as one safeguard and emphasize that people remain accountable for the work.
after.limitation: This is an account of a professional panel, not a controlled measurement of arbitration costs or outcomes.
